companies.credit_view: Amazon has swung from large net cash to a net-debt issuer in 12 months: face debt rose from $68.8B (YE25) to $133.0B (6/30/26) and ~$164B pro forma for July/September deals, while TTM FCF turned negative (-$7.6B) as net capex reached ~$169B and the 2026 guide was raised to ~$220B, so incremental AI capex is now explicitly debt-funded. Leverage is still low for an AA/A1 credit (gross debt/EBITDA ~0.9x; ~1.7x including ~$110B of lease liabilities, ~2.4x adding the $106B of signed-not-commenced leases), and EBITDA is growing fast (Q2 operating income +43% y/y, AWS +37%), but the trajectory is clearly negative and 2027 capex is guided up again. Headline earnings are flattered by ~$70B of non-cash Anthropic mark-ups in H1'26 that do not service debt. Prior 'net debt $50.7B' = non-current LTD $128.9B minus cash & equivalents $78.2B only (excludes marketable securities and $3.3B current portion) - not a like-for-like basis.

companies.covenants_and_key_terms: Senior unsecured notes; no financial maintenance covenants (standard IG - not re-verified). FY26 capex 'including finance leases' is Microsoft's reported capex metric (Q4 FY26 $41B incl. $5.6B finance leases; cash PP&E $35.8B); ltm_capex here is cash additions to P&E ($115,948M) and EXCLUDES finance leases.
companies.credit_view: Microsoft remains the strongest credit in the group: bond principal of ~$46.1B ($40.3B carrying) against $76.8B cash and short-term investments gives net cash of ~$31B on a principal basis (~$36.5B on carrying basis - this is the prior 'net debt -36.5B'), FY26 EBITDA ~$194B and FY26 FCF of ~$67B despite $116B cash capex, so it is not FCF-negative and guides positive FCF for FY27. The real leverage is in leases, not bonds: ~$88.5B of recorded lease liabilities ($66.6B finance) plus ~$329.1B of signed-not-commenced datacenter leases means lease-type obligations of ~$418B are ~9x bond debt; lease-adjusted gross obligations/EBITDA would be ~2.4x if all commenced. The pivot from finance to operating lease classification and the 15->25-year useful-life extension flatter reported capex and depreciation without reducing commitments - analysts should adjust. AAA/Aaa is secure given the cash generation, but the pace of lease commitments is the variable to watch.

companies.credit_view: Alphabet is levering up quickly in absolute terms - carrying debt reached $98.2B at 6/30/26 after ~$51.8B of H1'26 issuance across USD/GBP (incl. a 100-year bond)/CHF/EUR/JPY, and ~$123B pro forma for August's $25B deal - but it is the only hyperscaler funding the AI build with large amounts of new equity ($49.6B net in June; $84.75B program incl. ATM and Berkshire placement), which is strongly credit-protective. Headline net cash of ~$144.3B (= $242.5B cash & marketable securities less $98.2B debt) includes $87.1B of marketable equity securities; on a cash-and-debt-securities basis net cash is ~$57B. TTM FCF remains positive at $53.3B but Q2'26 FCF was -$5.9B and 2026 capex is guided to $195-205B with a further 'significant' 2027 increase, so FCF is likely to go negative on an annual basis. Off-BS lease commitments ($85.2B + $5.8B, plus any purchase commitments) are smaller relative to EBITDA (~$173B) than at MSFT or META; AA+/Aa2 looks well supported.

companies.credit_view: Meta is the most stretched of the four relative to its cash flow: long-term debt of $83.7B (after $30B in Oct-2025 and $25B in May-2026) is now roughly equal to $90.3B of cash and marketable securities (net cash only ~$6.6B, ~$17B counting $10.8B restricted funds), and Q2'26 FCF fell to $0.8B as capex incl. finance-lease principal hit $31.1B against $31.9B CFO - with 2026 capex guided to $130-145B, annual FCF is near zero and could turn negative. Off-balance-sheet obligations dwarf on-balance-sheet debt: ~$279B of signed-not-commenced leases at 6/30 plus ~$68B signed in July (~$347B), $349B of non-cancelable commitments, and ~$27B of Hyperion SPV bonds backed by Meta's lease and residual value guarantee - i.e., lease-like obligations of ~4-5x reported debt. Rating agencies have so far treated these as operating commitments; any agency move to capitalise leases/RVGs or a slowdown in ad revenue growth (+28% in Q2) is the key downside risk for AA-/Aa3.
